name: Middle cerebellar peduncle
summary: The largest of the three peduncles, a massive purely afferent bundle carrying the transverse pontine fibers from the contralateral pontine nuclei into the cerebellar hemisphere. It forms the lateral surface of the pons, with the trigeminal root emerging at its junction with the basis pontis. Infarcts here (AICA territory) or demyelination give ipsilateral limb ataxia, and bilateral lesions of the peduncles are a recognized pattern in multiple system atrophy and fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome.

anatomy.location: Lateral pons, sweeping backward and laterally from the basis pontis into the white matter of the cerebellar hemisphere, lateral to the superior and inferior peduncles.

function: Delivers the cortico-ponto-cerebellar input that lets the cerebellar hemispheres coordinate skilled limb movement planned by the contralateral cortex.

bestView.label: lateral pons at the trigeminal root entry, peduncle entering the cerebellum
middle peduncle from pons to hemisphere

imaging.normalAppearance: A thick band of white matter on the lateral pons on axial T2 and FLAIR; symmetrical T2 hyperintensity of both peduncles is a clue to multiple system atrophy (with the pontine 'hot cross bun') or FXTAS.

pathology.finding: Restricted diffusion in the middle cerebellar peduncle and adjacent lateral pons and cerebellum.
Symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintensity of both peduncles in multiple system atrophy (cerebellar type) or fragile X tremor/ataxia syndrome.
Peduncular plaque with ipsilateral ataxia, a common multiple sclerosis site.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: FLAIR and DWI through the pons and cerebellum

lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of pontocerebellar input to the ipsilateral hemisphere
Trigeminal root at the entry zone next to the peduncle

pearls: Bilateral symmetric bright middle peduncles in an older man with tremor and ataxia: think FXTAS
AICA infarcts typically cut the peduncle, so ataxia accompanies the deafness and facial palsy
